_meta.purpose: Per-service charge-type specification registry (Layer-1.5). ONE uniform schema for every AWS service: given a row whose service identity is already resolved (canonical_service, product_code-first), this declares the service's charge-types, how each is recognised, which reusable pricing mechanic prices it, and which fields it needs for full context. Replaces the greedy global regex rules in classify_mechanics.py with explicit per-service dispatch. The mechanic vocabulary (compute_breakdown/block_storage/...) is UNCHANGED — this only changes HOW a row's mechanic is chosen (per-service + explicit) instead of by global pattern order.
_meta.status: SEED — ec2 + rds only. Faithfully carried over from classify_mechanics.py RULES (each charge_type cites its source_rule). Field names grounded in the authoritative AWS CUR data dictionary. NOT YET consumed by any script. classify_mechanics.py still owns classification until the dispatch engine lands (see docs/SERVICE_SPECS_DESIGN.md migration plan). Grow one service at a time, ranked by spend.
_meta.evidence_source: Service seeding order = global spend ranking across all 75 historical job DBs (AGENTS.md global_sku_audit). Field names from AWS CUR product/line_item/pricing columns (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/table-dictionary-cur2-product.html) cross-checked against the columns ingest.py actually parses.
_meta.dispatch_model: canonical_service (identity, done) -> service_specs[canonical] -> test charge_types in order, FIRST MATCH WINS (same semantics as today's rule chain, but scoped to one service) -> assign (charge_type, mechanic) + compute field_state over the charge_type's fields. A row whose service has no spec here falls back to the legacy generic mechanic rules.

match_vocabulary._note: A charge_type matches when ALL present predicates are true. All regex are case-insensitive (re.IGNORECASE). Omitted predicates are ignored. This is a declarative mirror of the _ilike/_re/_is_hourly_unit helpers in classify_mechanics.py.
match_vocabulary.any_field_re: regex over '<usage_type> <operation> <product>' concatenation (for PDF/flat bills where the signal location varies)
match_vocabulary.exclude_usage_type_re: row does NOT match if this hits usage_type
match_vocabulary.exclude_operation_re: row does NOT match if this hits operation
match_vocabulary.unit_hourly: true => _is_hourly_unit(unit): unit in {hrs,hours,hour,hr,accelerator-hours,''} — '' included because PDF/flat bills leave unit blank

field_descriptor._note: Each field: name (internal), cur_column (authoritative AWS CUR attribute it comes from, legacy slash form as ingest.py uses; null = AWS does not expose it in the bill at all), source (where we REALISTICALLY obtain the value), required.
field_descriptor.cur_column: The AWS CUR column/attribute. null means AWS never bills this field — it MUST be enriched (api/llm).

source_enum.cur: present in the bill (ingest.py parses the cur_column directly).
source_enum.table: cur_column may be present but we derive authoritatively from a bundled table (ec2-instance-types.json / rds-instance-types.json / instance-specs.json) keyed by instance type.
source_enum.api: not in CUR; requires a live API / catalog sweep (gcp_sweep.py / AWS spec).
source_enum.llm: inferable only by LLM when cur+table+api all miss; cached to data/enriched_specs.json with confidence; lowest trust. NEVER overwrites a 'cur' value.
